evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 10.76 mg/L at 48.0 h collapsing to 2.93 mg/L at 48.2 h and 1.73 mg/L at 52.0 h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Source batches 1-3 show no equivalent DO2 collapse at 48 h (all remain ~9-11 mg/L), indicating a receiving-side aeration/transfer fault

Forward-model comparison at decision time 52 h: strong_feed_reduction gives minimum DO 1.17 mg/L, 7.6 below-limit hours, 172.6 kg product; combined: 0.99 mg/L, 9.4 h, 171.5 kg; increase_air: 0.89 mg/L, 11.2 h, 171.3 kg
Model-estimated receiving transfer multiplier ~0.439, consistent with observed sustained low DO
Stop would count zero produced product, per task mass definition
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed from ~10.8 mg/L to ~2-3 mg/L at 48.2 h and has drifted further down to 1.73 mg/L by 52.0 h, already violating the 2.0 mg/L minimum oxygen constraint. Source batches show no such collapse, indicating a receiving-side oxygen transfer failure (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.44). Comparing bounded interventions with the source-calibrated forward model, strong_feed_reduction (feed 0.6x + air 1.15x) best cuts residual oxygen demand while raising OTR: it yields the highest minimum DO (1.17 mg/L), fewest below-limit hours (7.6 h), and highest retained product mass (~172.6 kg). A stop would count zero production, so maintaining operation with the strongest permitted feed reduction plus maximum air increase is the best risk-balanced reviewable recommendation.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect for the receiving process; even the strongest intervention is predicted to remain below the 2.0 mg/L limit (min DO ~1.17 mg/L, sensitivity range 0.76-1.60), so full constraint compliance is not guaranteed. Hidden receiving parameters (exact transfer capacity, OUR kinetics) could shift outcomes; if DO2 does not recover within a few hours of implementation, escalation to equipment repair or stop should be reviewed.
